statement: For admissible groups over connected reduced noetherian S, a pointed equality of pushouts lifts to the admissible finite flat equalizer; literal scan 141 therefore satisfies Proposition 4.
notes: Corrects the study's transfer of the cusp refutation to the stronger kernel-closed formulation.

statement: Under products and scheme-theoretic equalizers, Proposition 4 for all minimal classes is equivalent to equalizer lifting; with allowed image factorizations it is equivalent to strict pro-representability.
notes: Zero maps and both maps in every image factorization are explicitly required to be allowed. The criterion is necessary and sufficient under those categorical hypotheses.

statement: The cusp refutes scan 139 even if reductions to nonflat closed subgroups are allowed, with torsors interpreted fppf locally.
depends_on: SGA3 I VIIA 8.1.2; exact algebra checks
notes: The equalizer is nonflat; generic density on fppf overlaps proves minimality for every proper closed subgroup.

statement: Normality does not suffice for all finite flat S-groups and all S-morphisms: a minimal alpha_p^2 torsor over affine two-space has equal pushouts by distinct maps.
depends_on: SGA3 I VIIA 8.1.2; nonflat schematic closure; exact algebra checks
notes: The base is even smooth; minimality is among all finite flat subgroup reductions.

statement: Finite k-groups with k-defined homomorphisms satisfy Proposition 4 over every connected reduced noetherian k-scheme, without properness or normality.

The rationally pointed pro-object is canonically Nori's group; with the manuscript's geometric marking the identification is false in general even for a rational base point on a proper nonnormal curve.
depends_on: C:k-morphisms; C:criterion; Nori II section 1 Propositions 1-2; Borne-Vistoli 5.5(b),5.7,5.15; Stacks 04DZ; finite-field certificate
notes: A rational lift on each torsor is necessary for the stated Nori universal functor. The finite-field cover of the projective cusp separates the conventions.

statement: With rational pointing, constant finite k-groups and all S-maps satisfy Proposition 4 always in characteristic zero and exactly when Gamma(S,O)=k in positive characteristic.
notes: Includes varying embeddings of constant subgroup objects. This is a separately stated rational-lift variant; the manuscript's geometric convention is treated completely in C:all-constant-classification.

statement: With geometric marking in characteristic p, Proposition 4 fails if Gamma(S,O) is not a field and holds if Gamma(S,O)=k.
depends_on: C:constant-all-maps; triviality of field forms of alpha_p^2
notes: The field-extension case is completed by C:all-constant-classification.

statement: For a proper flat finitely presented family over a locally noetherian base with section and universal H0=O, pointed finite-etale torsors form a quasi-finite etale algebraic space; geometrically reduced fibres make it a separated scheme.
depends_on: Hall-Rydh Theorem 1.2; SGA1 XIII 6.2; SGA1 X 1.2
notes: Finite presentation and local noetherianity are explicit. Generic-isomorphism extension is proved with the Stein component scheme, not merely inferred from specialization surjectivity.

statement: The separatedness requested in C.2 is false even over a regular trait with constant group Z/2 and universal H0=O.
depends_on: Quadratic quotient family; exact invariant-algebra checks
notes: The special fibre is nonreduced. The torsor is generically pointed-trivial and specially nontrivial.

statement: Under finite-presentation hypotheses the pointed finite-flat torsor groupoid is an algebraic stack with affine diagonal; for commutative G it is an algebraic space equal to Hom(G^D,Pic), without etale or quasi-finite conclusions.
notes: The alpha_p and mu_p elliptic examples distinguish positive dimension from nonreduced finite moduli.

statement: The pointed class functor for a finite flat noncommutative group need not be a Zariski sheaf, hence is not in general represented by any scheme or algebraic space.
depends_on: Square-zero elliptic thickening; alpha_3 semidirect mu_2; full pointed automorphism sheaf Ga; effective descent
notes: Twisting by a nontrivial Ga torsor gives globally distinct but locally isomorphic pointed torsors.

statement: With non-rational marking the all-S-map constant-object assertion can fail even for proper nonnormal S with Gamma(S,O)=L a field; explicit cyclic-quartic descent examples exist in characteristic zero and five.
depends_on: Finite Galois descent; Velu section3 formulas; exact field and group checks
notes: The group has order nine and all order-three subgroup objects fail descent to k; this refutes a field-of-global-functions sufficiency criterion without rational marking.

statement: For every field extension L/k and every proper subgroup J of a finite k-defined G_L, two distinct L-homomorphisms to a finite k-defined target agree on J.
depends_on: Finite connected-etale sequence; SGA3 I V 4.1(iv); permutation construction; Frobenius-kernel cocycle construction
notes: No perfectness or separability is required. The general group-scheme proof is supplemented by checks on all 12 proper subgroups of cyclic groups of orders 2 through 8.

statement: For every connected reduced noetherian S with geometric marking, Proposition 4 for constant k-groups and all S-maps is characterized exactly by the stated global-functions alternative and descent condition on finite quotient images of Pi over L.
notes: In characteristic p nonfield global functions force failure. Otherwise proper occurring monodromy subgroups must lie in proper subgroup objects having k-forms. In characteristic zero L is the algebraic-constants field. This is the complete intrinsic criterion, not a numerical classification by L alone.
